record.original_question: Construct a holomorphic minimal foliation, or a holomorphic minimal lamination, on a compact complex manifold that has uncountably many mutually singular extremal directed currents which are ddc-closed but not closed.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Construct holomorphic minimal foliation (resp. lamination) on a compact complex manifold with uncountably many extremal ddc-closed, non-closed, currents directed by the foliation (resp. lamination).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold equipped with a holomorphic foliation (possibly with singularities) $\mathcal{F}$, or more generally a holomorphic lamination, which is minimal in the sense that every leaf is dense in $X$. A positive current $T$ of bidimension $(1,1)$ on $X$ is said to be directed by $\mathcal{F}$ if, on every flow box, $T$ is a combination of integration currents along the plaques weighted by a positive transverse measure. The current $T$ is called $dd^c$-closed if $dd^c T = 0$, and closed if $dT = 0$. The current $T$ is extremal in the cone of positive $dd^c$-closed directed currents if it cannot be written as a non-trivial convex combination of two non-proportional such currents. Two positive currents are mutually singular if their trace measures are mutually singular Borel measures on $X$.

Construct an example of a compact complex manifold $X$ together with a holomorphic minimal foliation (respectively, a holomorphic minimal lamination) on $X$ admitting uncountably many mutually singular extremal positive directed $dd^c$-closed currents, none of which are closed.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Related work (e.g., unique ergodicity results for generic holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler surfaces) actually points in the opposite direction by showing uniqueness of directed positive $dd^c$-closed currents in many settings, making the construction of examples with uncountably many extremal such currents an outstanding question. No published construction matching the stated requirements was found.

status_evidence.title: Unique Ergodicity for foliations on compact Kähler surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: For generic holomorphic foliations on compact Kähler surfaces with hyperbolic singularities and no directed positive closed currents, there exists a unique positive ddc-closed (1,1)-current directed by the foliation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results establish uniqueness rather than multiplicity of directed ddc-closed currents in generic settings, indicating the asked construction is not yet realized.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems on Holomorphic Foliation Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 7.1. Construct holomorphic minimal foliation (resp. lamination) on a compact complex manifold with uncountably many extremal ddc-closed, non-closed, currents directed by the foliation (resp. lamination).
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem.
